prompt: Image 1 is a LAYOUT TEMPLATE: 10 plain grey shapes on a pure magenta ground. Each grey shape is one separate body part of a cut-out animation puppet, all seen from straight in front. Image 2 is the KEY to the template: the same layout, with each shape coloured to say which part it is (the key's colours are labels only: never paint with them). Image 3 is the character, drawn from straight in front: Juno, a 15-year-old girl: tan skin, short choppy teal hair with one long side lock hanging in front of her right ear, a small scar through her left eyebrow, round brass flight goggles pushed up on her forehead, chunky headphones resting round her neck, an orange cropped flight jacket with a high stand-up collar worn open over a navy shirt, the jacket sleeves pushed up to the elbows, three plain geometric patches on the jacket (a circle, a square and a triangle in flat colours, no emblems, no text), dark-grey baggy cargo trousers with a cream stripe down the outside of each leg and a cargo pocket on each thigh, red-and-white high-top trainers with no logo, brown fingerless gloves. Paint over image 1: replace every grey shape with that part of the character from image 3, drawn from straight in front, filling exactly the position, size, angle and silhouette of its shape.  What each key colour means: LIGHT GREY in the key = her head with all her hair and the goggles on the forehead; the head only, cut cleanly under the jaw with NO neck and NO shoulders. PALE YELLOW in the key = her bare neck only: a plain tan-skin cylinder with nothing on it. DARK YELLOW in the key = the far half of the stand-up collar: the inside of the orange collar as it shows behind her neck, in the darker shade tone, with the dark headphone band lying along it. MID GREY in the key = her trunk from the collar down to the jacket hem: the orange flight jacket and the near half of its stand-up collar, with what this view shows of the navy shirt and the headphones resting on the collar; NO head, NO neck (the neck opening is empty: magenta shows through it) and NO arms: where an arm would join, draw only the jacket's round armhole seam. DARK GREY in the key = her hips only: the top of the dark-grey cargo trousers with the belt, from the waist down to a plain rounded bottom at the crotch; no legs. DARK GREEN in the key = an upper arm only: the orange jacket sleeve from the shoulder down to the pushed-up cuff at the elbow; no forearm, no hand. LIGHT GREEN in the key = a forearm and hand only: bare tan forearm from the elbow, plain rounded end at the elbow, brown fingerless glove, hand relaxed with fingers lightly curled. BROWN in the key = one red-and-white high-top trainer with white laces and a white sole, no logo, no marks, no leg in it. DARK BLUE in the key = an UPPER leg only, hip to knee, in the dark-grey cargo trousers: plain rounded ends at the hip and at the knee, NO cuff, NO ankle; the cargo pocket and the cream stripe are on the outer face of the leg only. LIGHT BLUE in the key = a LOWER leg only, knee to ankle, in the dark-grey cargo trousers: plain rounded end at the knee, gathered cuff at the ankle, no shoe; the cream stripe is on the outer face of the leg only. Where they are: Row 1, left to right: upper leg; head; lower leg; upper arm; forearm. Row 2, left to right: torso; pelvis; neck; shoe. Row 3, left to right: collar back. Rules: the result has exactly 10 parts, one per grey shape, each where its shape is. Never draw a part that has no shape: the empty magenta areas stay empty. Do not draw whole limbs, whole trousers or a whole body anywhere. Every part is a complete, separate drawing with a closed black ink outline all the way round, with a plain rounded end where it would join its neighbour; parts never touch or overlap. No grey shape may be left unpainted. Keep the ground pure flat magenta (#FF00FF) outside the parts: no shadows, no glow, no magenta inside any part. Every colour comes from image 3 only. Style: 1990s hand-painted cel anime, exactly like the style reference: clean black ink outlines of even weight, flat colour fills, exactly two tones per material (a base and one hard-edged shade), no gradients, no texture, no soft shading, no highlights bloom. No brand logos, no text, no letters, no emblems anywhere.
